messages.subject: Missing value error in GGIR part 5 with .cwa file
parts:
Hi all, 

I am fairly new to GGIR so please excuse me if this is a basic fix. I am trying to use GGIR version 3.1.2 to visualize Lux parameters from an Axivity .cwa file. I have tried on a different system and encountered the same error. I have restarted R and cleared the environment but the error persists. Would appreciate any assistance anyone can spare. I've attached a link to the code and file in the link below. Many thanks for the amazing work you guys do!

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/197kJ_k8UMmwO7Xe9mmPXtvrpCyUrv45V?usp=sharing. 

I've attached the error message below:
MM-40-100-400-T5A5Error during Analysis and Feature Extraction: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed Warning message: In g.plot5(metadatadir = metadatadir, dofirstpage = params_output[["dofirstpage"]],

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Missing value error in GGIR part 5 with .cwa file
parts:
Dear Sean,

You are no using GGIR as intended. I can run part 1 and 2 command below (... replaced by full path):

GGIR(datadir = "D:/.../Farrell2408/file/BlackoutBlindTest.cwa",
     outputdir = "D:/..../Farrell2408",
     studyname = "test",
     # do.LUX = TRUE, # This is not a GGIR parameter
     f0 = 1,
     f1 = 0,
     mode = 1:2,  # Import and preprocess data
     overwrite = TRUE,
     do.report = c(2), #c(1) makes no sense as part 1 does not generate report
     LUXthresholds = c(5, 100, 1000),
     LUX_cal_constant = 1.0,
     LUX_cal_exponent = 0.7,
     LUX_day_segments = c(6, 20),
     # ignorenonwear = FALSE,
     # windowsizes = c(900)  # this parameter makes no sense, windowsizes needs to be length 3.
     hrs.del.start = 20,
     hrs.del.end = 6)

The code you have comes with the risk that you are using parameters inconsistently across GGIR parts which is likely to cause errors.

When I then look at the output I see that the sensor has not been worn!



You need to do these checks yourself. GGIR is open-source software, it is your responsibility to do the research.

Vincent
